manifest.name: dsh-title-curator
manifest.description: Stable emoji session titles for DeepSeek Harness: category emoji + object｜goal, with manual-rename locks, idempotent evaluation and a backfill pass for sessions you already have.
manifest.author: dsh-title-curator contributors

bundle.text:
# Title curator bundle: watches live sessions and rewrites only the title
# metadata through the official sessionTitle.rename() API. The built-in title
# provider stays mounted; this row does not replace or disable core rows.
- insert:
    - id: title-curator
      name: 'dsh-title-curator'
      config:
        enabled: true
        debounceMs: 6000
        minIntervalMs: 90000

readme.text:
Stable, human-recognisable session titles for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

Every session ends up as `category emoji + object｜goal`, for example `🧩 邮箱注册｜验证码过期修复`. The naming policy is ported from [oil-codex-title](https://github.com/oil-oil/oil-codex-title); the scheduling, state machine and host integration are written against DSH's official session-title API.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

*Real sidebar capture (default width; the host truncates long titles).*

A sidebar full of "回应中文问候"、"继续修改" is useless once several projects run in parallel. This plugin keeps the title on the *main line of work* instead of the last sentence: the object stays stable, the goal updates only when the work actually changes, and anything you renamed yourself is never touched again.

| | |
|---|---|
| Trigger | `user/message` (debounced), `turn/end`, `session/created` (opening an old conversation), first `request/header` |
| Model | the session's own route via `ctx.llm.stream`, cheapest supported reasoning effort |
| Write | `ctx.sessionTitle.rename()`, metadata only — no message is added, nothing enters model context |
| Failures | silent: the current title stays, the reason goes to `audit.jsonl` |

Behaviour worth knowing:

- **Idempotent** — a content fingerprint (policy version + cwd + title + recent message hashes) skips unchanged opportunities without a model call.
- **Manual rename wins forever** — the plugin records the title event seq it wrote; any change afterwards locks the session permanently.
- **No duplicate titles** — a candidate equal to another live session's title is retried once with the conflict list, then dropped rather than decorated with a fake suffix.
- **Keep-only-when-compliant** — a `keep` answer against a title that does not match `emoji + object｜goal` is rejected and retried with explicit feedback.
- **Cheap** — pure acknowledgements ("ok", "thanks", "继续") skip the model, and a session is evaluated at most once every 90 seconds.

From GitHub:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:chancecc99-gif/dsh-title-curator
```

From a local checkout:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-title-curator
```

Restart the host afterwards (a new package needs a fresh module generation). Uninstall:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove dsh-title-curator
```

Titles already written are ordinary `session/title` events and survive uninstall.

Override the row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: title-curator
  config:
    enabled: true
    debounceMs: 6000

See [README.zh.md](README.zh.md) for the full table.

Only the last 5 **human** messages (600 chars each), the current title, the last cwd segment and up to 16 titles of other live sessions are sent to the model. Assistant answers, tool output, file paths and attachments are never included.

State lives in `$DSH_HOME/plugin-data/dsh-title-curator/` (`state.json`, `audit.jsonl`). Deleting it degrades safely to "never touch a user-sourced title".

- Only live sessions can be renamed: DSH exposes no public write path for a session that is not mounted. Opening a conversation triggers a pass; an untouched, never-opened session keeps its old title.
- Titles are metadata, not folders — the emoji is a visual group, not a category tree.
- A session with thousands of events costs one log scan per evaluation.

```sh
npm test   # 24 tests: validators, parser, assembler, fingerprint, decision table, end-to-end host fake
```
